# Jordan's Social Life — Current State

As of mid-September, Jordan's social world runs on three steady points: Mika, Dev, and — until her last day at Meridian on 8/28 — Lena. Mika remains the constant, the one who shows up uninvited with pad thai, signs Jordan up for things before there's time to object, and has a years-long habit of not believing Jordan's excuses. Dev has moved from a first-nervous-coffee-walk to something close to a real friendship, now including honesty about the bad days, not just the good ones. Lena, though no longer down the hall, has stayed in the loop by text and is actively working to pull Jordan toward a job at Northlight.

The throughline since late July has been a repeating pattern: something goes wrong at work, Jordan withdraws, and someone — almost always Mika, sometimes now Dev — pulls them back out, usually toward Groundwork and toward Coda. It started small: a run with Mika on 7/31 that turned into the idea that Coda might be a real portfolio piece, followed by Mikayla sitting with Jordan through a funk on 8/4. By 8/24, after the "under evaluation" news, the pattern was explicit and named — Mika showing up with food, no questions asked, and Jordan writing out the cycle plainly: work knocks him down, he isolates, someone comes to get him.

Dev entered the picture on 8/8, nervous first walk at Greenwood Park, talked into it by Mika. That relationship deepened through the open mic on 8/21, where Dev and Mika met and hit it off over Nigerian funk documentaries, and through Jordan's admission on 8/27 that the "swamped" excuse for bailing on lunch was a lie — the real story was a bad week. Dev's response ("I would rather know you're having a bad week") seems to have shifted something; by 9/3, Dev was testing Coda for real, and by 9/16, Jordan was sitting on Dev's kitchen counter listening to setlist run-throughs three days before Dev's gig, bringing along Dad's old guitar picks, which Dev folded into their practice without ceremony.

Music has become its own social thread, not just an outlet: the 8/17 living-room practice with Pepper "harmonizing," the shaky but real 8/21 performance of "Fast Car" at The Lantern with Dev and Mika in the crowd, and now a second open mic signed up for on 9/16 — the Fern, September 27th — after catching himself about to talk himself out of it again.

Lena's exit on 8/28 removed Jordan's one office ally, but she's stayed active from outside: texting support after the reorg news landed on 9/1, calling legacy marketing "the holding pen," offering to refer Jordan to Northlight, and checking in on 9/17 ahead of the portfolio presentation with a no-fuss thumbs-up.

**Open threads:** Dev's gig is September 19th — today. The Fern open mic is the 27th. Northlight interviews and the design-team presentation land the 24th, with a first chat with new manager Priya on the 21st, meaning the next ten days will test how the Mika/Dev support system holds up under real stakes, not just bad-day recovery.
